Hi Amy — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, and then next steps: 

1) Subprocessors: Redwood maintains a published subprocessor list. For Hosted and Dedicated we currently operate on "notice with opt-out" semantics for certain categories (e.g., managed infra), but we can offer stronger controls for Private/on-prem customers. For Private deployments we can include a "prior written consent" carve-out for any subprocessor that would process customer content outside the customer's VPC.

2) Telemetry for Private/on-prem: by default our Private package does not route customer application data off-prem. We do offer limited telemetry (agent health pings, anonymized usage counters) to support upgrades and operational alerts only with explicit configuration. Those pings do not contain customer content and are TLS-encrypted; retention defaults are 30 days but can be shortened to 7 days for regulated customers. We'll put this language in the DPA and an operational appendix.

3) Data transfers: we support SCCs (EU model clauses) and can incorporate them into the DPA execution flow. For Dedicated we can also offer regional routing controls to keep inference traffic within EU regions.

I've attached our redline of the standard DPA (Redwood_DPA_redline_v1.pdf) that marks the proposed Private/on-prem carve-outs and suggested subprocessor approval flows. Please route to your counsel and flag anything they need changed.

Next steps: if these headroom items look acceptable, I'll loop in Marissa (contracts) and Neha (privacy) to finalize the redline and prepare a DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,

1) Private/on-prem: we will include a contractual guarantee that the default agent configuration will not transmit inference request payloads or sensitive application logs off-host. 2) Subprocessor notification window: for Private/on-prem customers we are willing to accept a 45-day notice for subprocessors that could access customer metadata, coupled with an expedited remediation plan if BOH objects.
